explanations: They are divided into two families: the typical family Strigidae, and Tytonidae, which holds the barn and bay kinds.
Most are solitary and nocturnal; the northern hawk one is diurnal and the burrowing one is gregarious.
They are found in all regions of the Earth except the polar ice caps and some remote islands.
In English venery a group of them is called a parliament.
They are birds of the order Strigiformes: mostly nocturnal birds of prey with an upright stance, a large broad head, sharp talons and feathers adapted for silent flight.

sources.excerpt: Owls are divided into two families: the true (or typical) owl family, Strigidae, and the barn owl and bay owl family, Tytonidae.
Exceptions include the diurnal northern hawk-owl and the gregarious burrowing owl.
They are found in all regions of the Earth except the polar ice caps and some remote islands.
A group of owls is called a "parliament" in English venery.

Owls are birds from the order Strigiformes (), which includes over 200 species of mostly solitary and nocturnal birds of prey typified by an upright stance, a large, broad head, binocular vision, binaural hearing, sharp talons, and feathers adapted for silent flight.
